title: ison: an instrument said in JSON (JSON Instrument Object Notation)
description: An instrument as words rather than code: the sounds it takes (`sources`), the ways it is played (`modes`, chosen per note with the note's `variant`), how it is played (`play`), its level, its envelope and its continuous controls by name. It wraps sounds jmon/sound already plays; it contains none.

description.description: What the instrument is and how it is meant to be played, in the composer's words.

family.description: The instrument's family, for defaults a host may apply (bowed strings enter a little softer): "bowed strings", "plucked strings", "winds", "brass", "keys", "percussion", "voice", "synth", "noise"…

range.description: The lowest and highest MIDI notes the instrument plays.

words.description: Words to find it by: a timbre, a mood, a gesture.

sources.description: The sounds, by name. Each is a spec jmon/sound plays: `{ sf2, program?, bankSelect? }`, `{ sfz }`, `{ faust, params? }`, `{ gm }`, `{ type, options }` (a Tone synth), a drum kit.

mode.description: The mode a note plays in when it names none. By default, the first of `modes`.

modes.description: The ways of playing, by name. A note chooses one with `variant`. The first is the default.

source.description: Which source plays this mode. By default, the first source.

program.description: For a SoundFont source: the preset.

bankSelect.description: For a SoundFont source: the bank number inside the file.

keyswitch.description: For an SFZ source: the key switch that selects this mode.

controls.description: For an SFZ source: controller values that select this mode.

params.description: For a Faust source: parameter values of this mode.

options.description: For a Tone or sampled source: options of this mode, over the source's.

holds.description: How many seconds a note of this mode sounds before its recording ends. Absent or 0: indefinitely (the recording loops, or the source is a synth).

oneShot.description: The sound plays once and dies on its own (a pizzicato, a hit): never split into strokes.

vibrato.description: The vibrato the recording already has, described, so the play rules know what they have.

play.description: How the instrument is played: rules a host applies to a track's notes before it schedules them (jmon/sound's performIson). Each rule is optional.

bow.description: A note longer than a bow is played in equal strokes, a bow change between them.

max.description: How many beats a bow lasts at most. A stroke is also never longer than what its mode's recording `holds`.

gap.description: Beats of silence at a bow change.

change.description: The velocity of the strokes after the first, as a proportion of the note's.

vibrato.description: A stroke long enough plays in the vibrato mode, unless the note chose its own variant.

from.description: Beats from which a stroke takes the vibrato.

mode.description: The mode that has the vibrato.

stroke.description: The shape of a stroke, as the note's `dynamics`: the numbers `bow` in jmon/algo takes.

attack.description: Beats to the first level, at most a third of the stroke.

swell.description: How much the stroke grows: it starts at 1 - swell of the peak.

peak.description: Where the peak falls, as a fraction of the stroke.

fade.description: How much it eases off by the end: it ends at 1 - fade of the peak.

minDuration.description: Beats below which a stroke only gets a soft attack.

level.description: The instrument's level, calibrated so that it sits with the others.

db.description: A gain on the instrument's output, in dB.

velocity.description: How the written velocity reaches the source: "sqrt" for a source that hears velocity as MIDI does (40·log10), so that a written 0.5 sounds half as loud rather than a quarter.

envelope.description: An attack and a release, in seconds, replacing the source's own (SFZ sources).

controls.description: The continuous controls, by name: the controller number each one is (`cc`, always: a lane written by name is that controller move, for a player and for a MIDI file alike), where it lands in a Faust DSP if it does (`param`), its starting value (0 to 1), what it does. A piece drives one with an automation lane whose target is the control's name.
